q: Biotechnology combines biological sciences with _____ technologies.
e: Biotechnology combines biological sciences with engineering technologies. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Medical is not engineering.

q: Traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and _____.
e: Traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and beer. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. In bread making, yeast produces carbon dioxide, which makes dough rise, plus ethanol. Metal is not beer.

q: Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into _____.
e: Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into vinegar. Wine yeast uses oxygen first, then ferments anaerobically when oxygen is gone. Juice is not vinegar.

q: Modern biotechnology produces antibiotic _____.
e: Modern biotechnology produces antibiotic penicillin. Penicillin is an antibiotic originally from a fungus. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Paracetamol is not penicillin.

q: Human _____ producing genes are put into bacteria.
e: Human insulin producing genes are put into bacteria. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar. Glucose is different: glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Transgenic goats produce antibodies in their _____.
e: Transgenic goats produce antibodies in their blood. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body. Urine is different: urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons.

q: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce _____.
e: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce vaccine. Vaccines are an applied-biology tool for preventing infectious disease. Poison is not vaccine.

q: Microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and _____.
e: Microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and viruses. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi. Plants is not viruses.

q: Archea and bacteria are _____.
e: Archea and bacteria are prokaryotes. Prokaryotes such as bacteria and archaea lack a true nucleus. Eukaryotes is different: eukaryotes have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

q: Viruses reproduce inside living cell using _____ materials of host.
e: Viruses reproduce inside living cell using genetic materials of host. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell. Structural is not genetic.

q: Yeasts have single _____ cells.
e: Yeasts have single spherical cells. Filamentous is not spherical.

q: Microorganisms are cultured easily by using _____.
e: Microorganisms are cultured easily by using fermenters. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi. Microscopes is not fermenters.

q: Biofuel fermentation produces _____ which is distilled.
e: Biofuel fermentation produces ethanol which is distilled. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Fermentation is microbial chemical change of organic material, with or without oxygen in modern use. Methanol is not ethanol.

q: Ethanol is mixed with petrol to get _____.
e: Ethanol is mixed with petrol to get gasohol. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Kerosene is not gasohol.

q: In bread making, water activates _____ enzymes.
e: In bread making, water activates amylase enzymes. Amylase is the enzyme that hydrolyses starch. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Protease is different: proteases digest proteins to amino acids.

q: Yeasts ferment sugar to carbon dioxide and _____.
e: Yeasts ferment sugar to carbon dioxide and oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Ethanol is different: yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: Protein _____ holds carbon dioxide gas bubbles in dough.
e: Protein gluten holds carbon dioxide gas bubbles in dough. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Keratin is not gluten.

q: Dough is baked in oven at _____ to kill yeasts.
e: Dough is baked in oven at 200^ degrees extC to kill yeasts. 200^ degrees extC is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Milk is pasteurized at about _____ to kill bacteria.
e: Milk is pasteurized at about 90^ degrees extC to kill bacteria. 90^ degrees extC is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Starter culture turns lactose to _____.
e: Starter culture turns lactose to lactic acid. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Acetic acid is not lactic acid.

q: Lactic acid coagulates milk protein _____.
e: Lactic acid coagulates milk protein casein. Casein is the main milk protein that clots in cheese making. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Gluten is not casein.

q: In cheese making, _____ causes further coagulation.
e: In cheese making, rennet causes further coagulation. Rennet enzymes clot casein during cheese making. Trypsin is not rennet.

q: Grape juice is treated with sulphur dioxide to kill _____ yeast.
e: Grape juice is treated with sulphur dioxide to kill natural yeast. Natural classification tries to reflect real evolutionary relationships. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. Artificial is not natural.

q: Yeast respire aerobically until _____ is used up.
e: Yeast respire aerobically until oxygen is used up. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. Nitrogen is different: nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: Yeast cells die when alcohol content reaches _____.
e: Yeast cells die when alcohol content reaches 15%. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. 50% is not 15%.

q: Beer is made from barley grains which activate _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Beer is made from barley grains which activate protein -digesting enzymes. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Starch is different: starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin.

q: The sugary solution obtained from malted barley is called _____.
e: The sugary solution obtained from malted barley is called wort. Whey is not wort.

q: Wort is boiled with hops which give beer a _____ flavour.
e: Wort is boiled with hops which give beer a bitter flavour. Sour is not bitter.

q: Louis Pasteur described alcoholic fermentation as 'life without _____'.
e: Louis Pasteur described alcoholic fermentation as 'life without air '. Air of the atmosphere supplies oxygen and carbon dioxide for life. Fermentation is microbial chemical change of organic material, with or without oxygen in modern use. Food is different: agriculture and husbandry both serve food production, but they are different practices.

q: Fermenter tanks are made of stainless steel to withstand _____ effect.
e: Fermenter tanks are made of stainless steel to withstand corroding effect. Cooling is not corroding.

q: Hot _____ is passed into fermenter to sterilize it.
e: Hot steam is passed into fermenter to sterilize it. Water is different: water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.
